But requirement says relative_seek function must be available and allow seeking within a seekable stream relative to current position. So we need to implement relative_seek function in recipes.py and expose it. Also modify seekable to support relative seeking. Let's inspect current seekable implementation: it has seek(index) absolute. Need to add relative_seek(offset). Implementation: current index self._index; we can compute new index = self._index + offset. But need to handle negative offsets, boundaries: cannot seek before 0? Should raise ValueError? The requirement: "allow seeking within a seekable stream relative to the current position." Should be similar to standard file seek with relative offset. Also ensure relative_seek works on a seekable stream. Also the seekable class must support this relative seeking capability. So we add method relative_seek(self, offset). Implementation: if offset is negative: move backward; need to ensure not below 0. If offset positive: move forward; may need to consume. Use same logic as seek but with index=self._index+offset. But we must consider that _index may be None? In __next__, after peek, _index set. In peek, after retrieving next, if self._index is None: set to len(self._cache). Then decrement. So _index always defined after peek? In __next__, after retrieving item from _source, _cache.append(item); return item. _index remains unchanged? Actually _index is used to track position? In __next__, when _index is None: it just returns next item; but _index remains None? That seems odd. But peek sets _index. The seek uses _index. So relative_seek should rely on current index; if _index is None, we can compute index=0? Actually if no peek, _index None; but relative_seek should probably use current position (len(cache) if exhausted?). But requirement maybe simpler: relative_seek(offset) should call self.seek(self._index+offset). But if _index None, maybe treat as 0? Might need to support relative seek even if not peeked yet.
